Pappi speaks the Memullai formula.
Pappi speaks the same formula in an enclosure discussion.
Pappi addresses Bibi and then says a different Rav Pappa demurred.
Huna son of Rav Yehoshua speaks; compare his separate wording on 151a.
The second attached occurrence also names Huna son of Rav Yehoshua.
Read his comparison to the place named in Bereshit Rabbah and the insulting intent Rashbam ascribes.
The text names the people of Bei Mamal.
Rabbi Meir’s Mamla encounter explicitly raises descent from Eli.
Pappi calls Bibi bar Abaye mar.
Rashi explains mar here as my teacher.
Rashi gives cut short and truncated, and explicitly gives Abaye as Bibi’s father from Eli’s house.
Rashi gives hump, with a mound comparison.
Rashi offers two explanations: shortened lives in Eli’s house, and his own explanation from a term for a hump.
Bibi wishes to complete the year’s portions on the eve of Yom Kippur. The same passage specifies the otherwise compressed Chiyya of Difti notice.
Bibi uses the procedure just described, sees the demons, is harmed, and recovers after the sages pray for him.
The two Miriams and the messenger are distinct. This Bavli witness names Bibi bar Abaye.
Kahana’s objection and Bibi’s rejoinder follow the question in the previous unit.
Huna son of Rav Yehoshua proposes a reading; Bibi disputes it, referring to Rav Yosef as master.
One reading has an unnamed sage addressing Bibi. The alternate has Bibi addressing Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.
The Arukh explicitly ascribes the favorable reading to a Gaon and transmits Rav Pappa. It also gives a separate explanation about the house of Eli.
The Arukh calls Mamla a city and proposes that Memullai refers to it. Its chapter numeral reads 29 in the checked transcription; the corresponding Rabbi Meir passage is in Bereshit Rabbah 59.
Tosafot challenges Rashi’s explanation and proposes Mamla as a place, citing the Rabbi Meir episode.
The Bavli explicitly names Abaye as a descendant of Eli. Rashi applies that descent to his son Bibi. Heilprin identifies Bibi as a priest.
The first answer contrasts sacrifice and meal offering with Torah. Abaye’s separate answer adds deeds of lovingkindness.
The Bavli calls her son Rav Zutra bar Tuvya and shows her coming before Bibi after divorce.
Chiyya bar Rav of Difti recites Scripture to Bibi in the eves-of-Yom-Kippur discussion.
The checked Ein Yaakov prints Dimi parenthetically and Bibi in brackets. Heilprin calls Dimi a copying error.
Havot Yair independently quotes the Rama’s moral reading and likewise refers to Beit Yehudah and the Shlah. This link points to the intermediary, whose own work is named here in the note.
